# Independent audit: homothetic centroid defect

Audited source: homothetic-pair-centroid-defect-and-disjoint-star-budget.md.


The support-function cancellation in the homothetic containment is exact. In particular it controls \(m-c_j\in\delta K\), whereas the movement gauge uses the opposite vector \(c_j-m\); the factor \(d\) enters precisely through \(-K\subseteq dK\). Volume comparison establishes \(\delta\ge0\) before this cancellation is used.

For \(0<\theta<1\), the two actual retained copies have centroids averaging to the candidate \(c_j\), and both radii are multiplied by \(1-\theta\). Their containment is simply convexity with the same point \(k\in\partial K\). Homogeneity of the already audited paired-source bound gives the stated loss factor, without an independent regularity or differentiability claim. The zero and unit-gauge cases are treated separately.

The exact zero-depth statement for \(\theta\ge1\) is also sound. The candidate lies outside or on the boundary of the actual midpoint section of the two-source hull. A separating or supporting plane has nonzero continuous normal because the midpoint base is in the relative interior of the endpoint segment. Its endpoint sections are empty or supporting faces, of zero full fiber volume. This exact criterion is correctly distinguished from the possibly weaker conservative test \(d\delta/\rho\ge1\).

At one actual own-fiber centroid, ordinary Grünbaum and the pair contributions concern disjoint integer fibers, so the finite star sum is valid before taking any halfspace infimum. All vertical caps are retained. The alternate factor in volume variables and the condition \(a>\Gamma_d b\) are algebraically correct.

For the centered simplex, \(-v/d\) lies on the facet opposite \(v\), giving the exact displacement gauge \(d\delta/\rho\). At \(\delta=\rho/d\), the displayed cap has zero mass on both endpoint fibers. The original three fibers remain exact fibers of their full convex hull. Thus the coefficient \(d\) is necessary for this conservative factor. The finite support-vanishing branch has the correct barycentric cap orientation and volume.

Finally, the three-dimensional certificate has mass coefficient \(232/125\), strictly below the target coefficient \(233/125\), but the old midpoint has the separate proved budget \(3\Gamma_3V\). This is correctly stated as a shortfall of the particular own-centroid certificate, not a depth counterexample.

No correction is required.
